Public Documentation ​

Documentation for ComposableRecurrences's public interface.

ComposableRecurrences.ComposableRecurrences Module
julia
ComposableRecurrences

Fast, composable and differentiable recurrences and causal convolutions.

A recurrence steps a value forward from a window of its own past values, as in an autoregression. A causal convolution weights past inputs by a kernel, as in a delay. For a single series the two are

where is the output at time , a multiplicative input, the convolved input and the kernel weight on lag . Every operator is differentiable, and the README lists the automatic differentiation backends it is tested with.

Recurrence and Convolution are the operators. A plain array holds one set of coefficients: a kernel's lag weights, a coupling's S × S matrix or a modifier parameter's single value. PerStratum gives one set per stratum, Pairwise one per pair of strata and TimeVarying one per time. A stratum is one of S parallel series computed together, such as a place or an age group. Inputs, histories and outputs are strata × time arrays, or a vector for a single series. Time is absolute, counted from 1, and a call covers the times start:stop.

conceptone way
feedback recursionRecurrence(kernel; coupling, modifiers), lag 1 first
causal convolutionConvolution(kernel), lag 0 first
strataPerStratum(x), Pairwise(x)
time variationTimeVarying(x, Secondary())
multiplicative inputr(gain; ...)
additive inputadd =, before the modifiers
seed and resumehistory =, with_state, state =, seeded
modifiersDepletion, Redistribute, Add, Clamp, Transform
variantsstructs: Hazard(), Floor(), Primary()
extensiona type with a forward method for a role

To extend the package, define a type and add a ComposableRecurrences.forward method, and optionally a ComposableRecurrences.pullback! method, for its role (ComposableRecurrences.Step, ComposableRecurrences.Init or ComposableRecurrences.Pressure).

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
g = [0.1, 0.3, 0.6]
Recurrence(g)(fill(1.2, 10); history = ones(3))

Public API ​

ComposableRecurrences.Add Type
julia
struct Add{B}

Adds b to each stratum's value wherever the modifier sits in the tuple: after a ComposableRecurrences.Depletion, the added values are neither scaled by nor drawn from the pool.

For each stratum (one of parallel series) at absolute time ,

where is the value entering the modifier, the value it passes on and the parameter read at stratum and time .

b is a parameter: one value, PerStratum, TimeVarying (one per time, shared by every stratum) or TimeVarying(PerStratum(B)) with B strata × time, read at the absolute time. Alone, Add(TimeVarying(PerStratum(B))) gives the same values as passing B as add. The state is unused.

Arguments

  • b: the values to add.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
mods = (CR.Depletion(50.0, CR.Floor()), CR.Add(TimeVarying([1.0, 0.0, 2.0])))
Recurrence([1.0]; modifiers = mods)(1.0; history = [2.0], stop = 3)

Fields

  • b::Any: The values to add: one value, PerStratum or TimeVarying.

ComposableRecurrences.Allocate Type
julia
struct Allocate{T}

Rescales each group of strata to an exogenous total: the strata of a group keep their shares of the group's value and the group takes its total. A stratum is one of parallel series computed together, such as a place or an age group.

At absolute time , with stratum 's value after the earlier modifiers, the strata of group and its total,

with the machine epsilon of the buffer eltype, so the group sums of equal the totals wherever  . It is meant for non-negative values: a group sum at or below zero is floored to . The groups partition the strata; a stratum in no group is an ArgumentError. The groups are stored flat, in the fields strata (each group's strata in turn) and offsets (where each group starts), so the analytic adjoint sees only integer arrays and total. total is a parameter over groups, not strata: one value, PerStratum (one per group), TimeVarying (one per time) or TimeVarying(PerStratum(T)) with T groups × time, read at the absolute time. It reads every stratum of a group, so it is not pointwise, and it has no state. It composes with the other modifiers in tuple order: (Allocate(groups, total), Add(b)) adds b after the split. Its reverse pass, with the output cotangent and  , is

and on the floor ( ) the term drops.

Arguments

  • groups: a vector of index ranges or vectors, one per group, partitioning the strata.

  • total: each group's total.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
totals = [10.0 12.0 15.0 18.0; 2.0 3.0 3.0 4.0]  # groups × time
split = CR.Allocate([1:2, 3:3], TimeVarying(PerStratum(totals)))
Recurrence([0.6, 0.4]; modifiers = (split,))(fill(1.2, 3, 4); history = ones(3, 2))

Fields

  • strata::Vector{Int64}: The strata of every group, group by group.

  • offsets::Vector{Int64}: Group p is strata[(offsets[p] + 1):offsets[p + 1]].

  • total::Any: Each group's total: one value, PerStratum or TimeVarying.

ComposableRecurrences.Convolution Type
julia
struct Convolution{K} <: ComposableRecurrences.AbstractOperator

A causal convolution whose kernel starts at lag 0: each output weights the current and past inputs,

where is the output of stratum (one of parallel series) at absolute time , its input steps earlier, = kernel[l + 1] the weight on lag and the kernel length. for   comes from history and is zero before it. Strata do not mix.

A vector kernel is shared by every stratum, a PerStratum kernel is S × L, and a TimeVarying kernel is L × T or TimeVarying(PerStratum(G)) with G S × L × T, all lag 0 first. A TimeVarying kernel's indexing sets which time its column belongs to: with ComposableRecurrences.Secondary (the default) column weights the inputs reaching output , as above; with ComposableRecurrences.Primary column is the delay pmf of the input at time , which spreads forward through it, so the weight is   and input mass is conserved up to the window's end.

To weight lags from 1, as a renewal's force of infection does, prepend a zero: Convolution(vcat(0, g)) recomputes   from the outputs of a Recurrence with kernel .

Called as c(x; history = nothing, start = 1, stop), the call covers the absolute times start:stop:

  • x: the inputs, length T or S × T, read at absolute time t. The inputs before start come from x itself.

  • history: the inputs before t = 1, oldest first (any length m, or S × m); earlier inputs are zero. Not with a Primary() kernel, which has no column for them.

  • start: the first time; 1 by default.

  • stop: the last time; the length of x by default.

The output has the layout of x and length stop - start + 1.

Arguments

  • kernel: the kernel, lag 0 first.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
delay = [0.0, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2]         # P(delay = 0, 1, 2, 3)
Convolution(delay)(ones(8); history = ones(3))

Fields

  • kernel::Any: The kernel, lag 0 first.

ComposableRecurrences.Depletion Type
julia
struct Depletion{F, P, A, P0, R, V}

Susceptible depletion: each stratum's new values are drawn from a pool that starts at pool0 and shrinks by what is drawn.

For each stratum (one of parallel series) and absolute time from the call's first time ,

where is the value entering the modifier, the value it passes on, the pool after step , the starting pool pool0 ( by default), the population, the heterogeneity exponent and the form's forward(form, Step(), v, s, N, α).

The form is a variant struct that draws value v from pool s with population N and heterogeneity exponent α through forward(form, Step(), v, s, N, α): ComposableRecurrences.Hazard (the default), ComposableRecurrences.Floor, or a new type with that method. α > 1 depletes faster as the pool shrinks (heterogeneous mixing). The state is the pool; the hazard fraction divides by N whatever the pool starts at.

Arguments

  • N: the population, one value or PerStratum, constant over time: a TimeVarying N is an ArgumentError.

  • form: the depletion form; Hazard() by default.

Keyword Arguments

  • heterogeneity: the exponent α; 1 by default.

  • pool0: the starting pool, one value or PerStratum; N by default. A seed drawn from the pool is pool0 = max(N - sum(seed), 0).

  • removals: values taken out of the pool after each step's draw, capped by what remains; a parameter (one value, PerStratum, TimeVarying or TimeVarying(PerStratum(r))), or nothing for none.

  • protected: a ComposableRecurrences.Protected pool that the removals move into and that is drawn from at a relative susceptibility, or nothing for none.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
seed = [1.0, 2.0]
depletion = CR.Depletion(100.0; pool0 = 100.0 - sum(seed))
Recurrence([0.5, 0.5]; modifiers = (depletion,))(fill(2.0, 8); history = seed)

Fields

  • N::Any: The population, one value or PerStratum.

  • form::Any: The depletion form.

  • heterogeneity::Any: The heterogeneity exponent α.

  • pool0::Any: The starting pool, or nothing for N.

  • removals::Any: The removals, or nothing.

  • protected::Any: The protected pool, or nothing.

source
ComposableRecurrences.Device Type
julia
struct Device{B} <: ComposableRecurrences.Executor

Runs every index of a loop as one thread of a kernel on a device, such as a GPU: thread k computes

backend is a KernelAbstractions backend, such as CUDABackend(), and the arrays the loop reads and writes must live on it. Kernel launches on one device run in order, so a loop reads the writes of the loop before it; reading the result on the host waits for them. Needs KernelAbstractions to be loaded. Under the default Serial executor, operator calls on arrays that live on a GPU (with GPUArraysCore loaded) run their strata loops with it without being asked. Parts that index arrays on the host, such as dense and sparse couplings, Depletion and modifiers with a vector step, do not run on a device yet.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences, JLArrays, KernelAbstractions
const CR = ComposableRecurrences
y = JLArray(zeros(4))
ex = CR.Device(KernelAbstractions.get_backend(y))
CR.each!((k, y) -> (y[k] = k^2; nothing), ex, 4, 4, y)
Array(y)

Fields

  • backend::Any: The backend the loop's kernel runs on.
source
ComposableRecurrences.EXECUTOR Constant

The executor that operator calls use for their parallel loops, Serial by default.

Set it for a block of code with with; operator types do not change. An operator op gives the same output under any two executors e_1 and e_2:

Each operator call reads it once. Threaded needs every modifier the loops run, including user-defined ones, to write only its own stratum's slots. Forward-mode AD with dual numbers runs the set executor. Forward-mode AD that transforms the code runs serially whatever executor is set, as the supported backends do not differentiate tasks. Under reverse mode the operators' own rules run their forward pass with the set executor and their reverse pass on the calling task, because the reverse pass adds every stratum's terms into shared kernel and parameter cotangents. A NoAdjoint call that a reverse-mode backend differentiates directly runs serially whatever executor is set, as the supported backends do not differentiate tasks.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
using Base.ScopedValues: with
const CR = ComposableRecurrences
with(CR.EXECUTOR => CR.Threaded()) do
    CR.EXECUTOR[]
end
source

struct Init

The role of a modifier's initial state: forward(m, Init(), s, history) writes the state s (one entry per stratum, or two for a ComposableRecurrences.Depletion with a protected pool, allocated by the operator at its buffer eltype) from the full history, and returns nothing.

It sets the state before the first step of the call at ,

where is the whole history of length , not only the last values the recursion reads, and is the modifier's own map. The default is  .

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
s = zeros(2)
CR.forward(CR.Depletion(PerStratum([100.0, 50.0])), CR.Init(), s, ones(2, 3))
s

ComposableRecurrences.NoAdjoint Type
julia
struct NoAdjoint{O}

Wrap an operator so it is differentiated by the AD backend's own treatment of its forward loop, bypassing any hand-written adjoint.

Called exactly like the wrapped operator, it computes the same output,

for every input , so its gradient is the same quantity by a different route: the backend's derivative of the forward loop rather than the hand-written pullback. Useful to time a hand-written adjoint against plain AD, and to check the two gradients agree. Plain Enzyme reverse AD of a sparse coupling is wrong, so an active sparse coupling under NoAdjoint throws an ArgumentError with Enzyme.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
r = Recurrence([0.2, 0.3, 0.5])
ComposableRecurrences.NoAdjoint(r)(fill(1.1, 6); history = ones(3))

Fields

  • op::Any: The wrapped operator.
source
ComposableRecurrences.Pairwise Type
julia
struct Pairwise{A<:AbstractArray}

A Recurrence kernel for every pair of strata: adds leading S × S axes, so it is S × S × L.

Each stratum's pressure sums every stratum's past values through its own lag weights:

where = x[i, j, l] weights stratum 's output at lag in stratum , is that output at absolute time  , and replaces the coupled pressure of a Recurrence. A stratum is one of parallel series computed together. It is equivalent to Routes over all pairs, with a faster path: one route per pair (i, j), with kernel x[i, j, :] and a coupling that is the unit matrix at (i, j). The kernel already mixes strata, so the coupling must be I. TimeVarying(Pairwise(A)) has A S × S × L × T.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
P = fill(0.25, 2, 2, 2)
Recurrence(Pairwise(P))(ones(2, 4); history = ones(2, 2))

Fields

  • x::AbstractArray: The pairwise kernels, lag on the last axis.
source
ComposableRecurrences.PerStratum Type
julia
struct PerStratum{A<:AbstractArray}

A coefficient given per stratum: adds a leading strata axis to its slot.

A stratum is one of parallel series computed together, such as a place or an age group. As a Recurrence kernel it is S × L, one row of lag weights per stratum, and stratum convolves only its own past values:

with = x[i, l] the weight on lag , the output of stratum at absolute time   and the value passed on to the coupling. A Convolution kernel is read the same way from lag 0. As a modifier parameter it is a length-S vector, = x[i]. PerStratum(TimeVarying(x)) is the same object as TimeVarying(PerStratum(x)).

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
G = [0.2 0.8; 0.5 0.5]
Recurrence(PerStratum(G))(ones(2, 4); history = ones(2, 2))

Fields

  • x::AbstractArray: The coefficients, strata on the first axis.
source
ComposableRecurrences.PieceInterface Type
julia
    PieceInterface

An Interfaces.jl Interface with mandatory components (:forward,) and optional components (:pointwise, :nstate).

An operator, coupling, modifier or variant with forward for a role.

The mandatory component checks that forward runs and keeps to its role's conventions (outputs written into the leading arrays, inputs unchanged). The optional pointwise component checks that a modifier's vector step equals its scalar step on every stratum,

where is the modifier, and its value and state vectors at time and the number of strata. The optional nstate component checks the state length against ComposableRecurrences.nstate.

Test objects are Arguments(; piece, role, args), with kwargs for Run().

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences, Interfaces
CR = ComposableRecurrences
Interfaces.test(CR.PieceInterface, CR.Clamp; show = false)

Extended help

Mandatory keys:

  • forward: forward runs in its role

Optional keys:

  • pointwise: a vector Step matches the scalar Step on each stratum

  • nstate: Init and Step keep the state at nstate(m, S) entries

ComposableRecurrences.Primary Type
julia
struct Primary

The indexing of a TimeVarying kernel whose column τ is the kernel of the input at absolute time τ, which spreads forward through it.

For a Convolution with kernel length ,

where is the output of stratum at absolute time , the input steps earlier, and the weight on delay (kernel[l + 1]) in column , the column of the input's own time. When every column sums to one, each input's total is kept once all its delays fall inside the window. In a Recurrence with kernel length the input is the output itself, so each output keeps the kernel of the time it was produced:

where is stratum 's kernel convolution at time , its output steps earlier and the weight on lag (kernel[l]) in column . Only outputs at times from 1 have a column, so a seed of length needs start > m. Kernel slots only: anywhere else it is an ArgumentError.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
P = [0.6 0.2 0.4; 0.4 0.8 0.6]         # one delay pmf per input time
Convolution(TimeVarying(P, CR.Primary()))(ones(3))

# Cohorts from time 3 on transmit less.
K = [0.5 0.5 0.2 0.2 0.2 0.2; 0.5 0.5 0.2 0.2 0.2 0.2]
CR.seeded(Recurrence(TimeVarying(K, CR.Primary())), fill(1.5, 6); history = [1.0, 1.0])

ComposableRecurrences.Protected Type
julia
struct Protected{Σ, V0}

A protected pool for ComposableRecurrences.Depletion: the depletion's removals move into it, and it is drawn from at relative susceptibility .

At absolute time , for each stratum (one of the parallel series computed together, such as a place or an age group) with unprotected pool , protected pool , step value , population , heterogeneity and removals , the depletion form draws from the effective pool    and the pools lose the draw in proportion, then the removals move from to :

When   the draw comes from alone,   . A with    gives protection, and   makes the protected pool more susceptible than . With vaccine efficacy ,   with removals times the doses gives all-or-nothing protection, and    with removals equal to the doses gives leaky protection. A delay from dose to protection is a Convolution of the doses before the call. The derivative through and takes the active branch. The depletion's state holds for every stratum, then .

Arguments

  • σ: the relative susceptibility, one value or PerStratum, constant over time.

Keyword Arguments

  • pool0: the starting protected pool, one value or PerStratum; 0 by default.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
doses = TimeVarying(fill(5.0, 10))
leaky = CR.Depletion(1000.0; removals = doses, protected = CR.Protected(0.3))
Recurrence([0.3, 0.5, 0.2]; modifiers = (leaky,))(fill(2.0, 10); history = [5.0])

Fields

  • σ::Any: The relative susceptibility, one value or PerStratum.

  • pool0::Any: The starting protected pool, one value or PerStratum.

source
ComposableRecurrences.Recurrence Type
julia
struct Recurrence{K, C, M<:Tuple} <: ComposableRecurrences.AbstractOperator

A recurrence over strata whose kernel starts at lag 1, stepped from a window of its own past values.

At absolute time , each stratum's kernel convolution of its last values is mixed by the coupling, scaled by the gain (a multiplier on each step's value, such as a reproduction number) and shifted by the add input, then passed through the modifiers in tuple order:

for   (start, stop), where

  • is the output of stratum at time , one of strata (parallel series such as places or age groups); for   it is the history;

  • is the kernel's weight on lag , kernel[l], the same for every and unless the kernel is PerStratum or TimeVarying;

  • holds each stratum's kernel convolution and is the   coupling, weighting stratum in stratum ;

  • is the gain and the add input, and is the element-wise product;

  • is the value entering the modifiers, the value after the -th and that modifier's state after step ; with no modifiers  .

A Pairwise kernel replaces with  . kernel[l] weights , as a generation interval or AR coefficients are written: a recurrence has no lag 0. The kernel is a length-L vector shared by every stratum, a PerStratum S × L matrix, or a TimeVarying L × T or TimeVarying(PerStratum(G)) with G S × L × T. A TimeVarying kernel with ComposableRecurrences.Primary indexing reads the column of each output's own time,   in place of , so each output keeps the kernel of the time it was produced; its seed must sit at times from 1. A Pairwise S × S × L kernel (or TimeVarying(Pairwise(A))) weights every pair of strata and already mixes them, so its coupling is I. The coupling is I (or a scaled λ * I), any S × S matrix (dense, sparse, Diagonal), a TimeVarying S × S × T array, or any struct with forward on ComposableRecurrences.Pressure. Modifiers are structs with forward on ComposableRecurrences.Step and, for an initial state, ComposableRecurrences.Init.

Called as r(gain = 1; history, state, add = nothing, start, stop), the call covers the absolute times start:stop:

  • gain: a scalar, a length-T vector shared by every stratum, or S × T, read at absolute time t; one when left out.

  • history: the outputs at times start - m to start - 1, oldest first, length m for a single series or S × m; zeros when left out. The recursion reads the last L, and a history shorter than L is zero-padded. A modifier's Init sees all of it.

  • state: a ComposableRecurrences.State from ComposableRecurrences.with_state, to resume from it; not with history or start.

  • add: nothing, a scalar, length T or S × T, read at time t.

  • start: the first time; 1, or state.t when resuming.

  • stop: the last time; by default the common length of the time-indexed inputs (gain, add), required without one.

Every time-indexed array, kernels, couplings and modifier parameters included, must cover stop. The output is length stop - start + 1 for a single series or S rows of it; the history sets which, and the number of strata. The buffer eltype promotes ComposableRecurrences.param_eltype of every input and field, so Float32 inputs give a Float32 output and dual numbers pass through any slot.

Arguments

  • kernel: the kernel, lag 1 first.

Keyword Arguments

  • coupling: how the strata's kernel convolutions mix; I by default.

  • modifiers: a tuple of modifiers applied after the core of each step.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
g = [0.6, 0.3, 0.1]                   # weights on lags 1, 2, 3
K = [0.9 0.1; 0.2 0.8]
R = fill(1.1, 2, 10)
r = Recurrence(g; coupling = K)
y = r(R; history = ones(2, 3))

# Resume from the returned state over the same inputs.
y1, state = ComposableRecurrences.with_state(r, R; history = ones(2, 3), stop = 5)
y2 = r(R; state)
y ≈ hcat(y1, y2)

Fields

  • kernel::Any: The kernel, lag 1 first.

  • coupling::Any: How the strata's kernel convolutions mix.

  • modifiers::Tuple: The modifiers, applied in order after the core of each step.

source
ComposableRecurrences.Redistribute Type
julia
struct Redistribute{K<:(AbstractMatrix), E}

Moves a share of each stratum's values to others, conserving the total: a share of origin 's value is realised in destination instead.

For each stratum (one of parallel series) at absolute time ,

where is the value entering the modifier, the value it passes on, = K[i, j] the share from origin to destination , origin 's intensity at time and the arrivals, kept as the state. Summing over gives . The diagonal of K is not read: a stratum does not import from itself. The intensity ε belongs to the origin and is a parameter: one value, PerStratum, TimeVarying or TimeVarying(PerStratum(ε)) with ε strata × time, read at the absolute time. Place it before a ComposableRecurrences.Depletion to deplete each stratum's pool by what it realises; a modifier sees   , the gain times the coupled pressure plus the add input, so the add values move too.

Arguments

  • K: the S × S kernel, K[p, q] from origin q to destination p.

  • ε: the origin intensity.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
K = [0.0 0.3; 0.2 0.0]
r = Recurrence([0.5, 0.5]; modifiers = (CR.Redistribute(K, 0.1),))
r(fill(1.2, 2, 5); history = [1.0 1.0; 0.0 0.0])

Fields

  • K::AbstractMatrix: The kernel, K[p, q] from origin q to destination p.

  • ε::Any: The origin intensity: one value, PerStratum or TimeVarying.

ComposableRecurrences.Run Type
julia
struct Run

The role of an operator's whole call, forward(op, Run(), args...; kwargs...), which returns (y, cache); calling the operator lowers to it.

For inputs (the call's arguments and the operator's fields) it computes the output over the call's times  ,

with the operator's own maths (see Recurrence and Convolution); cache holds what the reverse pass needs, such as the ComposableRecurrences.State.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
y, cache = CR.forward(Recurrence([0.5, 0.5]), CR.Run(), fill(1.1, 4); history = ones(2))

struct Secondary

The default indexing of a TimeVarying coefficient: column t is read at time t.

For a kernel, the weight on lag of the output at time is

where is the kernel's weight on lag in column and is the absolute time of the output, counted from 1. A time-varying coupling or modifier parameter is likewise read as . This is the only indexing outside a kernel.

using ComposableRecurrences
TimeVarying([0.8 0.7; 0.2 0.3], ComposableRecurrences.Secondary())

struct Serial <: ComposableRecurrences.Executor

Runs every index in order on the calling task:

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
const CR = ComposableRecurrences
y = zeros(3)
CR.each!((k, y) -> (y[k] = k^2; nothing), CR.Serial(), 3, 3, y)

ComposableRecurrences.State Type
julia
struct State{H, M, T}

The state ComposableRecurrences.with_state returns with an operator's output, passed back as state to resume.

After a call that ended at absolute time it carries

where is the output at time (one entry per stratum), the number of kernel weights and the state of the -th of modifiers after the last step. history holds the last outputs, states each modifier's state and t the time of the next step,  . A call with state continues exactly as one call over both ranges would.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
r = Recurrence([0.5, 0.5])
y, state = CR.with_state(r, fill(1.1, 6); history = ones(2), stop = 3)
state.t, r(fill(1.1, 6); state)

Fields

  • history::Any: The last L outputs, in the history's layout.

  • states::Any: Each modifier's state.

  • t::Any: The time of the next step.

source
ComposableRecurrences.Step Type
julia
struct Step

The role of one step of a modifier, or of a variant inside its owner (a depletion form inside ComposableRecurrences.Depletion).

A modifier maps the step's values and its own state at absolute time to new ones,

where holds one value per stratum (one of parallel series), is the modifier's state after the previous step and its state after this one. A pointwise modifier acts on each stratum separately,  .

  • forward(m, Step(), v, s, t) updates the step's values v and the modifier's state s in place (one entry per stratum, or two for a ComposableRecurrences.Depletion with a protected pool) and returns nothing.

  • forward(m, Step(), v, s, t, k) is the scalar form for stratum k, returning (v′, s′); a modifier with ComposableRecurrences.ispointwise implements this one.

  • forward(form, Step(), v, s, N, α) draws v from pool s for a depletion form, returning (y, s′).

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
CR.forward(CR.Hazard(), CR.Step(), 2.0, 80.0, 100.0, 1.0)

Fields

source
ComposableRecurrences.Threaded Type
julia
struct Threaded <: ComposableRecurrences.Executor

Runs the indices of a loop in contiguous chunks, one task per chunk. With m chunks, chunk c covers

There are m = min(ntasks, n) chunks, with ntasks the number of threads unless it is set. A loop whose work is below min_work, or with one chunk, runs in order on the calling task, as Serial does. The threshold applies to each loop. Independent strata are one loop per call, but strata that mix through a coupling, a pairwise kernel or a modifier with a vector step are one loop per step, so such models gain only with many strata. Results are identical to Serial because each index writes only its own slots. Errors inside a split loop arrive wrapped in a CompositeException. On arrays that live on a GPU, Threaded spawns CPU tasks that index the arrays from the host; use Device there.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
const CR = ComposableRecurrences
y = zeros(4)
ex = CR.Threaded(; min_work = 0, ntasks = 2)
CR.each!((k, y) -> (y[k] = k^2; nothing), ex, 4, 4, y)
y

Fields

  • min_work::Int64: The smallest loop work that is split across threads.

  • ntasks::Int64: The most chunks a loop is split into; 0 uses the number of threads.

source
ComposableRecurrences.TimeVarying Type
julia
struct TimeVarying{I, A}

A coefficient that changes over time: adds a trailing time axis to its slot.

Column of the array holds the coefficient for absolute time , counted from 1, so a resumed call carries on through the same array. With the default indexing the step at time reads ; a Primary() kernel's weight on lag is read from column  :

A kernel is L × T, or TimeVarying(PerStratum(G)) with G S × L × T. A Recurrence coupling is S × S × T. A modifier parameter is length T, or TimeVarying(PerStratum(B)) with B S × T.

The indexing sets which time a kernel's column belongs to, and is held as a type parameter so nothing branches on it:

  • ComposableRecurrences.Secondary (the default): column t weights the inputs reaching output t. This is the only meaning outside a kernel.

  • ComposableRecurrences.Primary: column c is the kernel of the input at time c, which spreads forward through it. In a Recurrence the input is the output at time c, so each output keeps the kernel of the time it was produced.

The two agree for a fixed kernel.

Arguments

  • x: the coefficients, time on the last axis, or a PerStratum of them.

  • indexing: Secondary() (default) or Primary().

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
G = [0.8 0.7; 0.2 0.3]  # lags 1 and 2 over two steps
Recurrence(TimeVarying(G))(1.0; history = [1.0, 1.0], stop = 2)

Fields

  • x::Any: The coefficients, time on the last axis.
source
ComposableRecurrences.Transform Type
julia
struct Transform{F, P, D}

Maps each stratum's value through a function f, with optional parameters θ. A stratum is one of parallel series computed together, such as a place or an age group.

At time , for each stratum ,

where is the stratum's value when the modifier is reached (after the modifiers before it in the tuple), its value after, and the unused state. is θ read at stratum and absolute time , as every modifier parameter is: one value , PerStratum(θ) giving , TimeVarying(θ) giving , or TimeVarying(PerStratum(θ)) giving . A tuple or NamedTuple of these is read entry by entry, so f receives a tuple or NamedTuple of scalars. Without θ the map is  .

The reverse pass, for output cotangent , is

with the partial derivatives from derivative when given, or else from a local forward-mode derivative of f. derivative(v) returns without θ, and derivative(v, θ) returns , the second shaped as . Values captured inside f (a closure, or a callable struct with float fields) are not in : without derivative the Recurrence holding such a map is differentiated by the AD backend instead, so they keep their gradients.

Scope: Recurrence; pointwise; analytic adjoint from the local forward-mode derivative or derivative.

Arguments

  • f: the map, called as f(v) or f(v, θ).

  • θ: the parameters, or nothing.

Keyword Arguments

  • derivative: the derivative of f, or nothing for the local one.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
# Iterate a probability generating function, q_t = G(q_{t-1}) from q_0 = 0:
# q_t is the probability that a negative binomial branching process has
# died out by generation t.
G(s, θ) = (θ.p / (1 - (1 - θ.p) * s))^θ.r
q = CR.Transform(G, (; r = 0.5, p = 0.4))
Recurrence([1.0]; modifiers = (q,))(; history = [0.0], stop = 6)
julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
# One saturation level per stratum.
sat = CR.Transform((v, c) -> c * v / (c + v), PerStratum([5.0, 20.0]))
Recurrence([0.5, 0.5]; modifiers = (sat,))(fill(1.5, 2, 6); history = ones(2, 2))

Fields

  • f::Any: The map, called as f(v) or f(v, θ).

  • θ::Any: The parameters, or nothing.

  • derivative::Any: The derivative of f, or nothing for the local one.

add_cotangent!(_::Nothing, v, idx...)

Add v to the mirror x̄ at index idx,

so the cotangents from every use of a parameter sum. This is x̄[idx...] += v for an array, x̄[] += v for a Ref (the index is ignored), the same into the array of a wrapper's (; x) mirror, and nothing for nothing.

Arguments

  • idx: the index into an array mirror.

using ComposableRecurrences
x̄ = zeros(2)

ComposableRecurrences.cotangent Function
julia
cotangent(_::Nothing, name::Symbol)

The cotangent of field name in the mirror x̄ of a struct, or nothing when x̄ is nothing or has no such field.

For a struct with fields and a scalar loss , the mirror holds

and this returns for the field named name.

A mirror holds a struct's cotangents for a ComposableRecurrences.pullback!: an array to accumulate into for a float array, a Ref for a float scalar, a NamedTuple of field mirrors for a struct ((; nzval) for a sparse matrix, (; diag) for a Diagonal, (; x) for a wrapper such as TimeVarying), and nothing where there is no cotangent.

ComposableRecurrences.each! Function
julia
each!(
    body,
    _::ComposableRecurrences.Serial,
    n,
    work,
    args...
)
julia
each!(body, ex::Executor, n, work, args...)

Call body(k, args...) for every k in 1:n with executor ex:

where each index k is one stratum (one of S series computed together, such as a place or age group), one series or one output time.

body must write only the slots it owns for index k, so the indices can run in any order or at the same time. A new executor type adds a method of each!. Returns nothing.

Arguments

  • body: the per-index function, called as body(k, args...).

  • ex: the executor that runs the loop.

  • n: the number of indices.

  • work: an estimate of the loop's total cost in inner operations, which an executor may use to run small loops in order; Serial ignores it.

  • args: the arguments passed to every call of body.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
const CR = ComposableRecurrences
# Row sums of a matrix, one row per index.
rowsum!(k, y, A) = (y[k] = sum(view(A, k, :)); nothing)
A = [1.0 2.0; 3.0 4.0]
y = zeros(2)
CR.each!(rowsum!, CR.Serial(), 2, length(A), y, A)
y
source
ComposableRecurrences.forward Function

Run x in role on primal arguments args.

For the role's inputs it computes its outputs

with the map each role's docstring gives: ComposableRecurrences.Run an operator's whole call, ComposableRecurrences.Step a modifier step  , ComposableRecurrences.Init an initial state from the history and ComposableRecurrences.Pressure a coupling  . Array outputs are written into the leading array arguments and the method returns nothing; a scalar ComposableRecurrences.Step returns its new scalars and ComposableRecurrences.Run returns (y, cache). To extend the package, define a type and add this method for its role: ComposableRecurrences.Step and ComposableRecurrences.Init for a modifier or variant, ComposableRecurrences.Pressure for a coupling.

Arguments

  • x: the operator, coupling, modifier or variant.

  • role: Run(), Step(), Init() or Pressure().

  • args: the role's arguments.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
struct Offset
    b::Float64
end
CR.ispointwise(::Offset) = true
CR.forward(m::Offset, ::CR.Step, v, s, t, k) = (v + m.b, s)
Recurrence([0.5, 0.5]; modifiers = (Offset(1.0),))(1.0; history = ones(2), stop = 4)
source
ComposableRecurrences.ispointwise Function
julia
ispointwise(m) -> Bool

Whether modifier m acts on each stratum separately.

A pointwise modifier's step factorises over strata (the parallel series): at absolute time , stratum 's new value and state depend only on its own,

This sets which ComposableRecurrences.Step a modifier implements: a per-stratum map sets ispointwise(m) = true and implements the scalar forward(m, Step(), v, s, t, k), which the default vector step loops over strata; a modifier that couples strata implements forward(m, Step(), v, s, t) instead. The default is false.

Arguments

  • m: the modifier.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
ComposableRecurrences.ispointwise(nothing)
source
ComposableRecurrences.nstate Function
julia
nstate(m, S) -> Any

The number of state entries modifier m keeps for S strata.

A stratum is one of the parallel series computed together, such as a place or an age group. The recurrence allocates each modifier's state with

passes it to the modifier's ComposableRecurrences.Init and ComposableRecurrences.Step, and checks a resumed state against it. This is the extension point for a modifier that holds more than one stock per stratum: a depletion with a protected pool keeps the unprotected pool then the protected pool,  . A pointwise modifier (ComposableRecurrences.ispointwise) keeps one entry per stratum, so it must have  .

Arguments

  • m: the modifier.

  • S: the number of strata.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
leaky = CR.Depletion(100.0; removals = 1.0, protected = CR.Protected(0.3))
CR.nstate(CR.Clamp(0.0, 1.0), 3), CR.nstate(leaky, 3)

ComposableRecurrences.param_eltype Function
julia
param_eltype(x) -> Type{<:Real}

The element type the parameters of x contribute to an operator's buffer.

The buffer eltype is the float promotion of this over the kernel, coupling, modifiers, inputs and history,

where is param_eltype, so a dual number or a Float32 anywhere sets it. The default recurses by value through fields, tuples and named tuples, so abstractly typed fields count; a Real gives its type and an array of reals its eltype. Add a method for a type whose parameters this does not reach.

Arguments

  • x: any object, such as a modifier, coupling or kernel.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
struct Scale
    a
    extra::NamedTuple
end
ComposableRecurrences.param_eltype(Scale(1.0f0, (; b = 2)))

ComposableRecurrences.pullback! Function

Accumulate the reverse pass of ComposableRecurrences.forward for x in role.

For forward computing outputs   from inputs and the object's parameters , given the output cotangent (the gradient of a scalar loss with respect to ) it adds

grads is a NamedTuple: grads.piece holds , mirroring the object's parameters (or is nothing), and the other fields are named after the role's arguments. Output cotangents are read on entry and input cotangents accumulated; a buffer forward updated in place is overwritten with the cotangent of its incoming value, and a scalar Step returns its input cotangents instead. Declare ComposableRecurrences.uses_adjoint for the same role so an operator's native rule calls it. Without one, a pointwise modifier with only scalar float parameters is differentiated locally with ForwardDiff, and any other object makes the AD backend differentiate the whole operator.

Arguments

  • grads: the cotangents, (; piece, ...), with piece the mirror of x's parameters.

  • x: the operator, coupling, modifier or variant.

  • role: the role.

  • args: the primal arguments forward was given.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
m = CR.Clamp(0.0, 1.0)
grads = (; piece = (; lo = Ref(0.0), hi = Ref(0.0)), v = [1.0, 1.0], s = [0.0, 0.0])
CR.pullback!(grads, m, CR.Step(), [0.5, 2.0], [0.0, 0.0], 1)
grads.v, grads.piece.hi[]
source
ComposableRecurrences.seeded Function
julia
seeded(r::Recurrence; ...)
seeded(r::Recurrence, gain; history, kwargs...)

Run r from a seed and return the seed followed by the run.

With a seed   placed at times it returns

where for   is the output of r started at    from history , and is the last time. Equivalent to cat(history, r(gain; history, start = m + 1, kwargs...); dims = ndims(history)): the time-indexed inputs are full length, their first times covering the seed. A seed shorter than the kernel is zero-padded.

ComposableRecurrences.test_adjoint Function

Test the analytic adjoint of piece in role on the primal arguments args with the AD backend's own rule tester.

The tester checks the pullback against finite differences of the forward map  : for random directions and cotangents ,

with from finite differences and from the pullback.

For an operator, role is ComposableRecurrences.Run and args are its positional arguments. Methods come from package extensions: AutoMooncake with Mooncake loaded (Mooncake.TestUtils.test_rule) and AutoEnzyme with EnzymeTestUtils loaded (test_reverse, with the operator active and constant).

Arguments

  • backend: an AutoMooncake or AutoEnzyme from ADTypes.

  • piece: the operator.

  • role: Run().

  • args: the positional arguments.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
methods(ComposableRecurrences.test_adjoint)

ComposableRecurrences.uses_adjoint Function
julia
uses_adjoint(piece, role) -> Bool

Whether piece carries its own analytic adjoint in role: a ComposableRecurrences.pullback! method for that role.

For outputs   of the role, with inputs and parameters , a declared adjoint computes the cotangents

by hand, where is the gradient of a scalar loss with respect to .

The author declares it next to the pullback! method; the default is false. An operator uses its adjoint in ComposableRecurrences.Run when it declares it; a Recurrence does when its coupling does in ComposableRecurrences.Pressure and each modifier does in ComposableRecurrences.Step or is pointwise with only scalar float parameters (those are differentiated locally per value). Otherwise the whole operator is differentiated by plain AD of its forward loop, logged once per operator type.

Arguments

  • piece: the operator, coupling, modifier or variant.

  • role: the role.

Examples

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
CR.uses_adjoint(Recurrence([0.5, 0.5]), CR.Run())

ComposableRecurrences.with_state Function
julia
with_state(op, args...; kwargs...)

Call operator op and return its output with the ComposableRecurrences.State to resume from, (y, state).

For a call over absolute times it returns

where is the output at time and the state after the last step (the last outputs, each modifier's state and  ).

Takes the same arguments as calling op; resume with op(...; state).

Arguments

  • op: the operator.

  • args, kwargs: the call's arguments.

julia
using ComposableRecurrences
CR = ComposableRecurrences
r = Recurrence([0.6, 0.4])
R = fill(1.1, 8)
